LESSON: INTEGERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Integers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Integers, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use integers in real life situations? 2. How do we carry out operations of integers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify integers in purposive pairs/ groups or individually by carrying out activities involving positive and negative numbers and zero. For example, climbing upstairs (positive), going down stairs (negative). Others may include standing at a point (the zero point) and count the number of steps moved either forward or backward and record. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (use residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/ write) to express their views. Observe safety precaution for learners such as those with weak bones against fractures as they perform the task.

2. draw/ trace in purposive pairs/ groups or individually and represent 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify integers in purposive pairs/ groups or individually by carrying out activities involving positive and negative numbers and zero. For example, climbing upstairs (positive), going down stairs (negative). Others may include standing at a point (the zero point) and count the number of steps moved either forward or backward and record. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (use residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/ write) to express their views. Observe safety precaution for learners such as those with weak bones against fractures as they perform the task.
2. draw/ trace in purposive pairs/ groups or individually and represent 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Integers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination- creating games: as the learner plays creative games that involve number lines, for example

jumping steps.

• Learning to learn: as the learner represents integers on the number line.

• Digital literacy- interacting with technologies: as the learner uses IT devices to learn and play games on integers.

Values

• Respect: as the learner works with peers to play games that involve integers.

• Unity: as the learner works together in creating games on integers.
